title: analytics: the ObjectQL strategy refuses a cross-object filter ("cb_order.status"), so a dashboard over detail rows cannot exclude rows of cancelled parents
body:
Found while landing steedos-labs/os-project-blackcat-crm#116 (PR #118) on the published 18.4.0 packages. The ObjectQL lines below are unchanged on `main` at `87330e89`.

## Symptom

A dashboard over child rows cannot exclude rows by a status on their parent. The downstream app's Order Margin dashboard and Allocation by Plant tile read allocation plans and plan lines. Both must leave out plans of cancelled orders, which means filtering on the order's status.

The dataset query with that filter:

```
POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query
dataset: cb_plan_metrics
runtimeFilter: { plan_kind: 'recommended', 'cb_order.status': { $ne: 'cancelled' } }
```

It answers `400 INVALID_FIELD`: `ObjectQLStrategy cannot evaluate a cross-object filter ("cb_order.status") — the engine cannot join in an aggregate`. Measured on the booted app with the sqlite driver.

## Producer

`packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts` (~line 1385, the `nonDim` check) refuses any cross-object measure or `where` filter. Its message reads "Run this query on a native-SQL driver". It does not say which deployments get the native strategy, or whether a two-hop path (plan line → plan → order) is reachable there at all.

## Why it matters

Any app whose figures live on detail rows, while their validity lives on the parent (cancelled orders, voided documents, closed periods), cannot keep those figures honest on a dashboard. The only app-side route is to copy the parent's status onto every child row. That is the kind of denormalised workaround the downstream repo's rules forbid while a platform answer is pending.

## Ask (for the lane to judge)

1. Say which drivers and deployments evaluate a cross-object `where` (native strategy), and whether multi-hop paths are in scope.
2. Either support a cross-object filter in the ObjectQL strategy (for example, resolve the parent ids first, then filter the base object by `IN`), or document the limit in the dataset authoring rules, so apps do not author dashboards that cannot be filtered.

Dedupe: `"cross-object filter" analytics`, `"cannot join in an aggregate"` and `ObjectQLStrategy join aggregate` among open issues. Nearest hits are #28557, #31842, #31881, #25814 and #28258, all closed and all about dotted-member resolution, not a refused cross-object filter. **New.** Dedupe words: analytics cross-object filter, ObjectQLStrategy join aggregate, runtimeFilter parent status, INVALID_FIELD cross-object.
